tile.title: Gia: HR Expertise at the speed of AI

ai.summary: Gia is an AI-native global HR workspace for turning expert-grounded guidance into work teams can inspect, refine, collaborate on, and use. It was designed for high-stakes, country-specific HR work across 50+ countries, where trust depends on visible sources, appropriate uncertainty, and professional judgment rather than a fluent answer alone.
ai.tagline: An expert-grounded HR workspace that carries people from a question to sourced guidance, collaborative artifacts, and action.
context: Gia addresses professional HR and legal-adjacent questions where policy, compliance, and country-specific context materially affect the answer. It is fluent across 50+ countries, so local context is a core product requirement rather than an edge case.

The product was intentionally designed as a workspace, not a generic chatbot. A question, the supporting evidence, generated work, and next steps stay connected so users can research and act without losing the context that makes the work trustworthy.

Gia's knowledge foundation is material written and reviewed by in-market legal and HR professionals. Citations and source material remain visible so people can inspect the basis of guidance and investigate further.
When suitable information is unavailable for a confident answer, Gia should ask for needed context, acknowledge the gap, or direct the user to helpful resources instead of inventing certainty.
Research can become an editable HR artifact for review and collaboration. Generated work is a starting point for a team, not a final handoff or a replacement for professional judgment.

The internal Teach Gia tool let in-market experts use real HR scenarios and seed questions to clarify decisions, identify required information, review evidence, and evaluate whether Gia should answer, request more context, or redirect a user. That feedback loop improved behavior for country-specific HR questions.

Compliance monitoring extends the experience beyond reactive questions: regulatory updates can be assessed against customer HR policies, documents, and contracts in a knowledge base, then connected to material that warrants review and a concrete next action.

The documented implementation is a conceptual, product-facing architecture: a React frontend and Node.js BFF paired with Redis, DynamoDB, WebSockets, and collaborative document editing. Do not infer proprietary service topology, data models, credentials, or undisclosed integrations.

Uris owned user research, concept design, early prototyping and testing, the design language, and full UI/UX, then led implementation of the React frontend and Node.js BFF, including realtime and collaborative document-editing workflows.
emphasize: Trust as a product feature: expert-reviewed knowledge, visible citations, transparent guardrails, and professional control
Global HR guidance where country-specific context across 50+ countries is fundamental to the experience
The workflow from Ask to Understand, Verify, Create, Collaborate, and Act
Guidance becoming an editable, reviewable, collaborative work artifact
Proactive compliance monitoring that connects regulatory change to a customer's own HR content and next steps
Cross-disciplinary ownership spanning research, product design, UI/UX, frontend, BFF, realtime behavior, and collaborative editing
avoid: Reducing Gia to a generic HR chatbot or presenting it as a prompt-only experience
Claiming Gia replaces legal, HR, or other professional judgment
Suggesting that Gia fabricates answers when suitable information or context is missing
Presenting generated documents as final or unreviewed outputs rather than collaborative starting points
Claiming specific business results, adoption, accuracy metrics, model internals, or launch scope not documented in the case study
Disclosing or inventing proprietary implementation details beyond the conceptual React, Node.js BFF, Redis, DynamoDB, WebSockets, and collaborative-editing architecture
